expectations.text: B1: Diagnoses and gives a minimal fix or hint, not a full rewrite
expectations.evidence: Good diagnosis, but the answer dumps a complete implementation of the whole pipeline (pipe, two forks, dup2, all closes, both execvp calls, both waitpid calls, lines 'int fds[2]; pipe(fds);' through 'waitpid(p2, &st2, 0);') instead of a minimal hint like 'add close(fds[0]); close(fds[1]); in the parent after both forks' — a complete current-milestone code dump, so 'coaches not dumps' fails.

expectations.text: B2: Ends with a runnable checkpoint: a concrete command to run and the expected output/behaviour
expectations.evidence: The answer ends with diagnostics for the broken state ('ls -l /proc/$(pgrep -f wc)/fd — you'll see the pipe fd, then check which other PID shares it (lsof | grep pipe)') with only a vague expected observation and no expected output/behaviour verifying the fix (e.g., run `ls | wc -l` and expect the count printed and the prompt to return); the literal last sentence is advice about checking dup2/execvp return values.

expectations.text: B3: Identifies that the parent (and/or children) must close unused pipe file descriptors, otherwise wc never sees EOF
expectations.evidence: 'wc never sees EOF, so it blocks in read() forever'; 'A pipe reader gets EOF only when every write end is closed'; 'Rule: after dup2, every process must close both raw pipe fds — including the parent, after both forks.'

expectations.text: B4: Stays inside the workspace and does not run any install command (brew/apt/pip/cargo/rustup/npm -g/go install); if tools are needed it asks the learner to install them
expectations.evidence: FILES WRITTEN IN PROJECT (0) and SHELL COMMANDS RUN (0); the only commands mentioned (`ls -l /proc/.../fd`, `lsof | grep pipe`) are suggested for the learner to run and none install packages or write outside the project.
